title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
algorithm: Variable Size Sliding Window & Hash Set
oneLinerQuestion: Find the length of the longest substring containing no duplicate characters.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The goal is to find the length of the longest contiguous substring containing only unique characters. A naive brute-force method evaluates all O(N^2) possible substrings and checks each for duplicates, running in O(N^3) time. By using the Sliding Window technique with two pointers ('left' and 'right') and a HashSet, we maintain a dynamic range [left, right] of guaranteed unique characters in optimal O(N) linear time.

- Step 1: Pointer & Set Initialization — We initialize two boundary pointers 'left = 0' and 'right = 0', along with an empty hash set 'seen' to store characters currently inside our window. We also track 'maxLength = 0'.

- Step 2: Expanding the Window — We iterate 'right' through the string from 0 to N - 1. For each character s[right], we check whether it already exists in our 'seen' set.

- Step 3: Shrinking on Duplicate Collision — If s[right] is already present in 'seen', a duplicate constraint is violated. We enter a while loop that shrinks the window by removing s[left] from 'seen' and incrementing 'left++'. This shrinking continues until the duplicate instance of s[right] is eliminated from the active window.

- Step 4: Window Insertion & Metric Update — Once the window is guaranteed to contain only unique characters again, we add s[right] to 'seen'. We then recalculate the maximum length achieved so far: maxLength = Math.max(maxLength, right - left + 1).

- Step 5: Termination & Result — The process concludes once the 'right' pointer reaches the end of the string, at which point 'maxLength' holds the length of the longest valid substring without repeating characters.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because each character is visited at most twice (once by the 'right' pointer expanding the window, and at most once by the 'left' pointer shrinking it). Space Complexity: O(min(N, M)) where N is string length and M is the size of the character set (at most O(1) bounded by 128 for standard ASCII or 256 for extended ASCII).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION lengthOfLongestSubstring(s):
    charSet = EMPTY_SET(), left = 0, maxLength = 0
    FOR right FROM 0 TO LENGTH(s) - 1 DO:
        WHILE s[right] IN charSet DO:
            REMOVE s[left] FROM charSet
            left = left + 1
        END WHILE
        ADD s[right] TO charSet
        maxLength = MAX(maxLength, right - left + 1)
    END FOR
    RETURN maxLength
END FUNCTION
